A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer block coupling study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original measurements of Jacobian coupling, hidden trajectories and training dynamics across LLMs, including extensive appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original LLM analyses and adds results from training 64 vision transformers, alongside new prompt and perturbation experiments.

M1.justification: The Jacobian/SVD coupling procedure and LSS/expodistance measurements are retained. Although v3 simplifies the top-K notation in Section 3.1, Section 5.4 and Appendix A.6 still refer to truncated calculations. The ViT experiments apply the existing analysis rather than introduce a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds CIFAR10 image classification, substantially extending the language-focused coverage of v2. It also evaluates difficulty-labelled Easy2Hard prompts and GSM8K prompts with appended zero-shot chain-of-thought instructions. The original leaderboard datasets and WikiText2 analyses remain.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks the coupling analysis against competing analysis methods. The new ViT sweeps and standard-versus-CoT probes compare experimental conditions. Compression, pruning and early-exit methods newly discussed in Table 2 are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a controlled 64-model ViT experiment with fixed architecture and an eight-by-eight weight-decay/stochastic-depth grid. It adds restricted-model regression subsets and embedding-noise testing. The Pythia coupling experiment also changes its reported checkpoint schedule and retains 6.9B/12B models while dropping the 1B series from that comparison.

E4.justification: New analyses examine regularization, model-size and score restrictions, training-token counts, prompt difficulty, CoT prompting and embedding perturbations (Figures 6–11, 15 and 30; Table 4). These substantially expand the questions tested. Conversely, the K=100 sensitivity panel and v2's Figure 29 misalignment maps are omitted; many other appendix analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v3 adds regression p-values for the full model sample and restricted subsets in Table 4, including 1.56×10^-6 for the full sample. Figure 5(b) also supplies uncertainty intervals for untrained expodistance, whereas v2's Figure 18 showed points without intervals. Existing LSS median/IQR reporting continues; no repeated-seed protocol is introduced.

E6.justification: The main correlation plot is revised from R²=0.7214 to 0.75, with changed plotted coupling values and model membership; this is not a same-setting performance gain. New ViT results report R² values of 0.35, 0.48, 0.74 and 0.83 at stochastic-depth rates 0, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.3. Additional findings include model-dependent CoT effects and perturbation responses. Table 1 and many earlier appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2's continuous-ODE motivation is replaced and expanded with finite-depth matrix products and spectral derivations. v3's Appendix A.5 derives conditions yielding ED=0 and LSS=1, while Section 6.2 adds a gradient-based optimization argument. Appendix A.6 also introduces computational-complexity analysis. These are substantive mathematical additions beyond notation changes.

C1.justification: The central claims about coupling, its correlation with generalization, and trajectory regularity remain. v3 adds adjacent-layer locality emerging through training to the contribution statement, refining the coupling claim without replacing the paper's central thesis.

C2.justification: v3 adds a subspace interpretation, an argument that stronger coupling complicates optimization, and an interpretation connecting stochastic depth to coupling. Table 2 claims implications for merging, pruning, projection, permutation and early exiting. Exponential growth is also qualified from occurring across all considered LLMs to occurring in the vast majority of trajectories; the heterogeneous-pretraining limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 supplies the new ViT experiment's architecture, hyperparameter grids, Adam learning rate, 500-epoch schedule, warmup, mixup, batch size, GPUs and training time. Appendix A.6 adds computational-cost details. Existing LLM hardware, batching, quantization and supplemental-code statements are retained rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens positioning through generalization bounds, dynamical isometry, subspace models, compression and early exiting, particularly in Sections 5.4–6.2 and Table 2. It adds associated references such as Arora, Pennington, Ashkboos and Gromov. The earlier information-processing subsection and its associated references are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, methods explanation, discussion and related work undergo substantial rewriting. Token-wise coupling is reorganized into self/context categories, linearity and exponential-growth results are combined, and the limitations and conclusion are condensed. These changes materially reshape the narrative beyond accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: v3 rebuilds Figure 1 as a five-panel overview, adds axes and colorbars to enlarged coupling displays, and combines/restyles regularity plots. It adds Tables 2–4 and multiple experimental figures, while moving several earlier main-text figures into the appendix and regrouping existing appendix panels. These are substantial visual and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2's central generalization evidence relied primarily on heterogeneous pretrained LLMs. v3 adds fixed-architecture ViT training experiments and restricted-model correlation checks, providing substantial controlled and size-restricted support for the central relationship. Detailed training instructions and clearer comparative figures improve reproducibility and assessment. The new compression and early-exit explanations in Table 2 exceed the experiments presented, and LLM causality remains unresolved, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger empirical foundation.
